title: Continuous-angle logical rotations in the Steane code
authors: Eric Huang, Daiwei Zhu, Matteo Ippoliti, Christopher Monroe, Michael J. Gullans
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate continuous-angle logical $Z$ rotations in the $[[7,1,3]]$ Steane code on the IonQ Forte trapped-ion processor. A round of the protocol applies a transversal physical $Z$ rotation by $θ$, followed by Steane syndrome extraction and decoding, which induces a syndrome-dependent logical $Z$ rotation. We analytically derive the effect of dephasing noise on the logical rotation angle and logical dephasing rate. Using logical Ramsey interferometry, we observe coherent syndrome-dependent logical rotations from a single round of the protocol. We find that the logical channel reconstructed from process tomography is a noisy logical $Z$ rotation well explained by a dephasing model. We further implement a two-round protocol applying physical rotations $+θ$ and $-θ$, and observe cancellation of the total logical angle with low logical dephasing for repeated trivial syndromes. This constitutes a proof-of-principle demonstration of continuously tunable non-Clifford logical gates by transversal rotations and standard error correction in a small quantum code.
summary: This paper reports an experimental demonstration of continuous-angle logical Z rotations using the Steane code on a trapped-ion quantum processor. By applying transversal physical rotations followed by syndrome extraction, the authors show that the logical operation is controllable and tunable. This work provides a key proof-of-principle for building fault-tolerant quantum computation using standard error correction techniques.
main_problem: The paper aims to experimentally demonstrate continuous-angle logical Z rotations within the Steane code, proving a method for continuously tunable non-Clifford logical gates.
main_result: The authors successfully observed coherent, syndrome-dependent logical rotations and demonstrated angle cancellation in a two-round protocol, confirming the feasibility of implementing tunable logical gates.
method: The protocol involves applying transversal physical Z rotations, followed by syndrome extraction and decoding, and characterizing the resulting logical channel using Ramsey interferometry and process tomography.
model_or_system: The experiment is performed on the IonQ Forte trapped-ion processor using the $[[7, 1, 3]]$ Steane code. The theoretical framework models the logical channel as a composition of rotation, dephasing, syndrome extraction, and correction.
key_observables: Logical rotation angle ($\phi_s$), logical dephasing rate ($q_s$), and syndrome-conditioned Ramsey fringe probabilities.
important_parameters: Physical rotation angle ($	heta$), dephasing noise rate ($p$), and the code parameters of the Steane code.
main_assumptions: The analysis primarily uses a dephasing-only error model, and the implementation is limited by the lack of mid-circuit measurement and feedforward on the hardware.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the single-round protocol showing theoretical dependence of logical rotation/dephasing on $	heta$ and noise; subsequent figures detail the two-round tomography circuit and plot the fitted logical rotation angle and dephasing parameter versus $	heta$.
paper_structure: The paper details the theoretical derivation of the logical channel action under noise, presents the single-round experimental demonstration using Ramsey interferometry, and concludes with a two-round protocol to test for angle cancellation and low dephasing.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses fault-tolerance and gate universality in physical quantum hardware, providing crucial experimental validation for theoretical concepts in quantum error correction codes.
